problems.reason: Both sentences state that pathologies on Cryolophosaurus bones show evidence of scavenging behavior.
Both sentences claim the crest was used for intraspecific recognition.
Sentence 21 classifies Cryolophosaurus as a derived neotheropod closely related to Averostra, while sentence 22 classifies it as a basal neotheropod.
Sentence 23 gives an age range of 186–182 Ma, whereas sentence 24 gives 196–188 Ma for the same species.

Sentence 26 says the classification remains debated due to mixed traits, while sentence 27 states new studies in 2007 demonstrated it was probably a ceratosaurian more closely related to Dilophosaurus and Dracovenator.
Sentence 28 challenges the idea that the crest was for mating, fighting, or intimidation, whereas sentence 29 disputes the species recognition function and suggests a socio‑sexual display model.

notes: - contradiction: "Cryolophosaurus is currently classified as a derived neotheropod closely related to Averostra." / "A 2020 study by Adam Marsh and Timothy Rowe classified Cryolophosaurus as a basal neotheropod.": Sentence 21 classifies Cryolophosaurus as a derived neotheropod closely related to Averostra, while sentence 22 classifies it as a basal neotheropod.

- contradiction: "Cryolophosaurus ellioti is the only known species of the extinct Cryolophosaurus genus, a basal dilophosaurid theropod that lived during the Early Jurassic, approximately 186 to 182 million years ago, in what is now Antarctica." / "Cryolophosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic Period, approximately 196 to 188 million years ago.": Sentence 23 gives an age range of 186–182 Ma, whereas sentence 24 gives 196–188 Ma for the same species.

- contradiction: "The classification of Cryolophosaurus remains debated due to its mix of primitive and advanced characteristics." / "However, new studies in 2007 demonstrated Cryolophosaurus was probably a ceratosaurian more closely related to Dilophosaurus and Dracovenator than to tetanurans.": Sentence 26 says the classification remains debated due to mixed traits, while sentence 27 states new studies in 2007 demonstrated it was probably a ceratosaurian more closely related to Dilophosaurus and Dracovenator.

- contradiction: "Researchers challenged the idea that the bizarre crest and armor of Cryolophosaurus were primarily for mating, fighting rivals, or intimidating predators." / "In 2019, the species recognition function of the crest was disputed, while a socio-sexual display model was suggested.": Sentence 28 challenges the idea that the crest was for mating, fighting, or intimidation, whereas sentence 29 disputes the species recognition function and suggests a socio‑sexual display model.
